variant: Rebuilt drum robot, as described at the FIRST in Texas District Championship; the team's earlier robot that season used a turret.

s5.title: Photo listed on The Blue Alliance

s6.title: 6369 Mercenary Robotics | Behind the Bumpers | FRC REBUILT Robot

bet.text: A drum instead of a turret: more throughput, less software, simpler and more reliable.

demand.text: Carry as much fuel as possible and empty it fast. The team wanted a full 12 in of hopper extension and a floor that moves fuel to the shooter in the least time, and calls the raised net very useful for overfill cycles over the bump.

auto.text: Autos run paths and then use the same auto-aim as teleop, so a path that ends a little off is corrected before shooting.

cycle.text: The slapdown intake lifts fuel high into the hopper, the rolling floor carries it to tilted transfer rollers, and a drum shoots it. One button points the robot with an X lock against defense; the flywheels are already at speed and the transfer starts on target.

endgame.text: None at the FIRST in Texas championship: the level 1 climber was taken off because the robot was overweight.

gave_up.text: The climber. The robot weighed around 105 lb in the shop with everything on it but about 124 lb at event check-in, so the climber was the first thing to go.

changed.text: The team rebuilt for the FIRST in Texas championship: a drum replaced the turret, and the slapdown intake was kept. This year it also swapped WCP swerve modules for SDS ones. Brass flywheels wore on the last robot, so this one uses stainless steel.

outcome.text: 77-9-0 in official play; ranked 16 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 292.81, Curie).

solves.text: Modules that are easy to replace, with enough speed and torque

facts.text: Swerve Drive Specialties MK5n modules at ratio 2, in place of WCP modules

functions.name: Intake

solves.text: Keep contact and compression on the fuel as long as possible

functions.type: three-bar slapdown intake with full ramp

facts.text: Three bars lift fuel high, so the rolling floor can empty the hopper with little help from the intake
It can push balls into the indexer
Its jackshaft is hidden inside a floor roller, so the floor keeps the full width

solves.text: Move as much fuel as possible to the shooter in the least time, by the simplest method the team saw on other robots

facts.text: Custom 3D printed stub rollers joined by 42-tooth belts
One roller pivots with the intake and spins with the floor

functions.name: Hopper

solves.text: Fit as much fuel as possible

functions.type: extending hopper with a raising net

facts.text: Extension, moving passively with the intake
About 50 to 55 balls with the net down and up to 78 with it raised, staying within 30 in

solves.text: Bring balls from the hopper into the drum channel

facts.text: Two 2 in rollers and one 1.25 in roller, on two Kraken X60s at about 1.33:1
The rollers tilt backward, so balls funnel passively from the hopper into the drum channel

solves.text: The drum alone did not have enough momentum to hold shot speed for around 60 to 70 balls

facts.text: 3 in aluminum drum on four Kraken X60s at 1:1
Stainless steel flywheel on the side, about
Two 1.25 in back rollers wrapped in silicone, with a polycarbonate hood ramp
The motors sit directly under the drum, leaving room for Limelights, battery and radio
Kraken X60 packaged behind the battery and under the ramp
Taken off at the FIRST in Texas championship because the robot was overweight

solves.text: Hold aim against defense, and correct small path errors in auto

facts.text: Three Limelight 4s give full-field position in auto and teleop
One button points the robot with an X lock; the transfer starts once on target, with flywheels already at speed
